laws.rule: Wakayama Youth Healthy Development Ordinance (和歌山県青少年健全育成条例), art. 22 (the ordinance says "night", 夜間). The ordinance sets the late-night period as 10 pm to 4 am. A guardian must try not to let a young person (generally under 18) go out in that period without special reason; the guardian's own duty has no penalty. Anyone else is barred from taking such a young person out, going about with them or keeping them out in that period without the guardian's consent or another proper reason. The offence for others carries a fine of up to JPY 300,000 (about A$2,707). Rates: RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = JPY 110.82.

items.text: The Wakayama Prefecture Youth Sound Development Ordinance (和歌山県青少年健全育成条例, Ordinance No. 36 of 19 October 1978) defines a young person, for chapter 3 onwards, as someone until they reach 18 (art. 8(1)). Article 28 forbids anyone, knowing that a listed act may be done to a young person or that a young person may do it, from providing a place for it or arranging that place. The listed acts include drinking alcohol or smoking (art. 28(4), as amended by Ordinance No. 12 of 2012). Article 29 also forbids soliciting, inciting or forcing a young person to do those acts, or giving money or other benefits in order to have them done. A breach of article 28 or 29 is punishable by imprisonment (拘禁刑) for up to one year or a fine of up to JPY 500,000 (about A$4,512), or as set out in art. 33(2). A person cannot escape that penalty by saying they did not know the young person's age, unless there was no negligence (art. 33(8)).

The same articles 28(4) and 29 of the Youth Sound Development Ordinance, and the same penalty of imprisonment for up to one year or a fine of up to JPY 500,000 (about A$4,512), also cover smoking by or involving a person under 18.

The Wakayama Prefecture Ordinance on Preventing Smoking by Persons Under 20 (和歌山県20歳未満の者の喫煙の防止に関する条例, Ordinance No. 31 of 24 March 2008, renamed and amended by Ordinance No. 54 of 24 December 2021, in force from 1 April 2022) adds duties that sit alongside the national under-20 smoking law. Unless it is clear that a would-be buyer is 20 or over, a seller must ask for the identification documents set in the regulation and check the person's age (art. 9). Tobacco vending machines must be able to confirm that the buyer is 20 or over, so that a person under 20 cannot buy; no one may transfer or lend the card or similar item needed to use such a machine to a person under 20 (art. 10). No one may ask a person under 20 to buy tobacco (art. 11). The governor is to request the measures needed to ban smoking on the grounds of schools and child-welfare facilities (art. 12). If a seller breaks article 9 or 10, the governor may issue guidance or a recommendation, and may publish the seller's name and the facts if the seller ignores a recommendation, refuses a required report, or obstructs an inspection (arts 13 to 16). This ordinance does not itself set a fine amount.

psychoactive-substances.notes: The youth ordinance regulates providing or arranging a place for someone under 18 to drink or smoke, and soliciting those acts. The smoking ordinance adds seller and vending-machine duties for people under 20. These are not a restatement of Japan's national under-20 drinking law as prefecture law. Yen converted at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026 (A$1 = JPY 110.82).
